name: Input
description: Single-line text entry. Also styles <textarea> and <select>.

states.name: error
states.description: The value is invalid. Adds a heavier bottom edge so the state does not rely on color.
states.pair: Set aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing at the c-form-field__error message.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The field cannot be edited. Rendered ghosted with a dashed keyline.

whenToUse: One line of free text: a name, an email address, a search query, a number.
Multi-line text on a <textarea>, or a choice from many options on a <select>.
whenNotToUse: Choosing among 2 to 6 visible options: `c-radio` buttons read faster than a select.
A yes/no choice: `c-checkbox`, or `c-toggle` when it applies straight away.
Showing a value that cannot change: plain text, not a read-only input.
use: Always wrap in c-form-field with a c-form-field__label.
Use the right type attribute (email, tel, number, search) so mobile keyboards match.
avoid: Using placeholder text as the only label.
Setting a width on .c-input; it fills its container. Constrain the container instead.

do.text: Give every input a visible label that stays visible while typing.

dont.text: Don't use the placeholder as the label: it disappears as soon as someone types.

do.text: Pair the error state with aria-invalid and link the message with aria-describedby.
do.html: Enter a start date after 1 January 2020.

dont.text: Don't show an error with a red border alone.

content: Error messages say what went wrong and how to fix it: "Enter a date after 1 January 2020", not "Invalid date".
Show errors when the person leaves the field or submits, not while they type the first value. Once a field is in error, clear the message as soon as it is fixed.
Mark the few optional fields with "(optional)" in the label; don't add asterisks to required ones.

a11y: Every input needs a programmatic label: <label for> on c-form-field__label.
Error text must be linked with aria-describedby, not only shown in red.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into and out of the field.
